lead.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin meet for 90 minutes in Shenzhen with little to show, and Putin vows a "far more painful" answer to Ukraine
lead.short: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for 90 minutes in Shenzhen on Thursday, the first meeting of the three leaders. Putin called it "a new page in the history of diplomacy", but it produced little of substance. Afterwards he vowed that Russia's answer to Ukraine's strikes on the Crimea bridge would be "far more painful".

why.text: It showed the US, China and Russia meeting as a club of great powers, with Europe and Ukraine outside the room.

more: Trump, who was seen falling asleep during the main APEC session, greeted Putin almost as a wartime ally, the Guardian reported. Putin said Europe's efforts to isolate Russia had failed, called a meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin a sideshow, and said his relationship with Trump rested on "similar civilisational values". For Xi, it was a chance to play host to both.

Ukraine hit the Crimea bridge for a third time this week early on Thursday, using Neptune cruise missiles, after Tuesday's strike collapsed its central road section. Putin claimed the bridge carried only civilian traffic and ruled out a truce on Black Sea shipping or energy targets. Kyiv's defence ministry said the strikes meant "time gained and lives saved".

facts.Crimea bridge: hit a third time this week

update.new: The summit is held, and Putin threatens retaliation.
update.front: The three leaders met for 90 minutes, and Putin then promised a harsher answer to Ukraine.

seconds.headline: Anthropic shares close 17% up at about $97 on their Nasdaq debut, valuing it at $1.75 trillion as Wall Street falls
seconds.short: Anthropic's shares closed about 17% higher at around $97 on their first day of trading on Thursday, up from the $83 listing price, valuing the Claude maker at about $1.75 trillion. They opened at $111.50, briefly valuing it at about $2 trillion. The gain came as the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 both fell more than 2%.

why.text: It is the first of the leading AI model makers to list, and its strong start did not stop a wider sell-off in AI-linked shares.

more: Investors set aside the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble. The S&P 500 fell for a fifth straight session. The listing made thousands of Anthropic employees millionaires and rewarded the venture capitalists who backed a company founded five years ago by former OpenAI staff worried about AI safety. It raised a record $81.3bn.

Asian shares headed for their worst week since 2020 as the AI rout deepened, with South Korea and Taiwan hit hardest. Jefferies strategist Christopher Wood raised India's weight in his Asia portfolio by one percentage point to 15% and cut Taiwan by the same amount, his second increase for India in three weeks.

update.front: Anthropic's shares rose 17% on their first day, even as Wall Street fell.

seconds.headline: Jaiswal's 85 and a 130-run opening stand take India to 159 for one, after Nicholls's 175 helps New Zealand to 368
seconds.short: Yashasvi Jaiswal made 85 off 89 balls and shared an opening stand of 130 with KL Rahul as India reached 159 for one at stumps on the second day of the first Test in Wellington, 209 behind. New Zealand were bowled out for 368, with Henry Nicholls unbeaten on 175 and Glenn Phillips making 118.

why.text: India had let New Zealand recover from 70 for five on the first day, so the openers' reply keeps the match even.

more: Jaiswal, tentative early, attacked after tea, taking 30 runs off the 21 balls he faced from Jacob Duffy and hitting 16 fours in all. Rahul played closer to his body and also reached a half-century before the close. Devdutt Padikkal is next in.

Phillips, who resumed six short of a century, reached it with a drive off Prasidh Krishna before Akash Deep bowled him. He became only the second batter, after Rohit Sharma, to score centuries in all three formats against the same opponent in a calendar year. Jasprit Bumrah took four wickets as New Zealand added 125 to their overnight score.

update.front: India's openers put on 130 in reply to New Zealand's 368.

seconds.headline: Cyclone Akvan crosses the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha and weakens, after more than 3 lakh people are moved
seconds.short: Cyclone Akvan began crossing the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coast early on Friday, made landfall near Gopalpur, and weakened into a deep depression over south coastal Odisha by 11.30am, the IMD said. Odisha moved more than 3 lakh people to safety and deployed 423 rescue teams, and heavy rain is falling along its coast.

why.text: It is the third cyclone to hit Andhra Pradesh in a month, and Odisha's coastal districts are taking the heavy rain.

more: The landfall process could take seven to eight hours, said Manorama Mohanty, director of the Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre. The storm was moving north-northeast at 24 km/h and is expected to weaken into a depression within six hours, and into a well-marked low-pressure area six hours after that.

Earlier forecasts had it crossing the Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni. Rough seas hit the coast at Aryapalli in Ganjam district, and heavy rain flooded low-lying parts of Ichchapuram and Sompeta in Andhra Pradesh's Srikakulam district. The Odisha Assembly was adjourned for two days, and legislators were asked to help people hit by the storm.

update.front: Akvan has now come ashore in Odisha, where more than 3 lakh people were moved.

stories.headline: Britain and the EU are set to agree a youth scheme for up to 100,000 young people a year at Friday's summit
stories.short: Up to 100,000 young people from the EU would be able to travel, work and study in Britain each year, and the same number of Britons in Europe, under a youth mobility scheme set to be agreed at the UK-EU summit in Brussels on Friday, the BBC understands. Downing Street said talks were "down to the wire".

why.text: It is Britain's biggest step back towards Europe since Brexit, under a prime minister who says the country lost more than it gained.

more: Andy Burnham says a "Channel action plan" on migration could also be agreed, and negotiators are working on food trade rules and carbon pricing. Britain's demand to cap numbers has been a sticking point, as has the EU's request that its students pay the same university fees as British ones. Britain already has such schemes with 13 non-EU countries, including India.

Labour rejected an EU proposal for an open scheme for 18 to 30-year-olds in 2024, calling it a return of free movement. "What's in it for us is the possibility of lower food prices," Burnham said, adding that he would walk away if he had to. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused him of "reopening the divisions" of the referendum.

stories.headline: The rupee rises past 93 a dollar for the first time since April, and the Sensex gains 0.9% to a three-month high
stories.short: The rupee strengthened past 93 to the dollar on Friday for the first time since 20 April, touching 92.91 in early trade and about 92.77 by 2pm, a gain of more than ₹1 this week. Foreign buying of Indian shares and bonds and steady oil prices helped. The Sensex rose 0.9% to 83,777, and Nifty Bank 2.2%.

why.text: A stronger rupee eases the cost of imported oil, and foreign money is moving into India as investors sell AI-heavy markets such as Taiwan and Korea.

more: "Exporters, if they get the upside beyond 93.50, should sell for their exports with higher premiums, while importers may now wait to buy near to 93.00 levels," said Anil Kumar Bhansali of Finrex Treasury Advisors, who pointed to sustained foreign buying of Indian shares behind a Sensex rally of nearly 1,000 points. Markets are pricing in US rate rises in December and January after the Fed's October minutes, which has kept the dollar firm elsewhere.

Precious metals kept falling. Gold and silver exchange-traded funds fell by up to 6.4% in early trade, with Nippon India's silver fund at a 52-week low, and 24-carat gold in India fell 5.8% to ₹1,23,580 for 10 grams. US gold futures traded about 4% lower, near $3,530 an ounce.

stories.headline: GTA 6 takes an estimated $2.36bn in pre-orders and first-day sales, the biggest entertainment launch ever
stories.short: Grand Theft Auto 6 sold more than 24.5 million copies in pre-orders and first-day sales, taking about $2.36bn, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower, which would make it the biggest entertainment launch in history. This year's highest-grossing film, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, made $2.5bn in its whole cinema run. Rockstar called demand "unprecedented".

why.text: A game that took 13 years and more than $1bn to make has taken more than twice its cost in its first day.

more: About three-quarters of sales were for the PlayStation 5 and the rest for Xbox, Sensor Tower said, basing its estimates on email receipts and public gaming profiles. Niko Partners expects the game to make more than $3bn this year. Sensor Tower says it will cut the time players spend on other single-player games by 10%.

Rockstar and its parent Take-Two have not released sales figures. The game follows Lucia and Jason, two small-time criminals in Leonida, a Florida-inspired state. Its budget of more than $1bn makes it the most expensive video game ever made, and it is the first new GTA game since GTA V in 2013.

stories.headline: Alcaraz has an MRI scan on his left thigh but is expected to play Cobolli today, a day before the semi-finals
stories.short: Carlos Alcaraz had an MRI scan on his left thigh on Thursday, after needing strapping during his win over Daniil Medvedev, and cancelled training. Spain's Cadena COPE reported that he should still play his last group match against Flavio Cobolli on Friday at 18:30 IST, though the scan results have not been made public.

why.text: A tear would probably end his season, costing him a first ATP Finals title and a Davis Cup campaign with Spain the following week.

more: He also had tape on his right knee before the Medvedev match, and the scans covered both. He has already topped his group, so the Cobolli match matters little; his semi-final is scheduled for Saturday. A withdrawal would still end his tournament. Alexander Zverev has also reached the semi-finals.

Alcaraz missed last year's Davis Cup Finals with a hamstring injury in his right leg picked up at the same event. He has won 11 matches in a row this autumn, including titles in Vienna and Paris, and has lost only twice in 24 matches since returning from a wrist injury at the US Open in August.
